issues.description: Audio format hardcoded by f-string from sample_rate with no validation against allowed values
issues.detail: User passes sample_rate=11025 or 32000 and you happily build 'pcm_11025' which the server will reject. The STTAudioFormat Literal lists exactly six values, but nothing enforces them. Either validate against the literal set and raise immediately, or accept audio_format as a parameter. Don't let the type system lie.

issues.description: Error message types raise from inside recv_task but the exception is swallowed by bare except
issues.detail: _process_stream_event raises APIConnectionError on auth_error/quota_exceeded/etc, but recv_task wraps the call in `except Exception: logger.exception(...)` and continues. So the connection error is logged and the loop keeps spinning forever on a dead session. Either re-raise APIConnectionError specifically, or set a flag and break.

issues.description: Reconnect loop never actually reconnects on send/recv task failures
issues.detail: The outer `while True` only loops when _reconnect_event is set, but nothing sets it. If send_task or recv_task raise, tasks_group completes with an exception, `task.result()` re-raises, and the function exits. So 'reconnect' is dead code, and a transient network blip kills the stream. Either wire up reconnect on failure or delete the scaffolding.

issues.description: Parameter validation ranges documented in docstring but not enforced in code
issues.detail: Docstring says vad_silence_threshold_secs must be 0.3-3.0, vad_threshold 0.1-0.9, durations 50-2000. None of these are checked. The user finds out via a WebSocket disconnect with an opaque server error. Validate at __init__ and raise ValueError with the actual bounds. Cheap, obvious, and saves the next maintainer a support ticket.

issues.description: Shadowing builtin `stt` module name with `stt` parameter
issues.detail: SpeechStreamv2.__init__ takes a parameter named `stt: STTv2`, but the file imports `from livekit.agents import stt`. Inside __init__ the module is shadowed. It happens to not bite here because the module isn't used in __init__, but it's a trap waiting for the next edit. Rename to `stt_instance` or pass it positionally as the parent class expects.

issues.description: No tests added, justified by 'Deepgram did it too'
issues.detail: 'The other guy skipped tests' is not a reason; it's evidence the codebase has a problem. A streaming protocol with state machine transitions (partial/committed/empty-commit, speaking flag) is exactly what regresses silently. At minimum add a unit test that feeds canned WS messages through _process_stream_event and asserts the event sequence. That's an hour of work and catches real bugs.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch is the right shape — a separate STTv2 class mirroring the existing Deepgram pattern, WebSocket streaming, sensible chunking — and the diff is readable and scoped. But it has two real bugs the author should fix before this lands: the sample_rate-to-audio_format conversion lies to the type system and will silently produce invalid pcm_ strings, and the reconnect scaffolding is dead code because nothing ever sets _reconnect_event on task failure. Documented parameter ranges aren't enforced, which is the kind of trivial omission that generates avoidable support load. The 'tests are broken so I skipped them' justification is not acceptable for a stateful streaming protocol; a small unit test over _process_stream_event would catch real regressions. Fix the validation, fix the reconnect, add one focused test, and this lands.
